PullRequest.Title: agentHost: honor saved allow rules when the Assisted reviewer requires approval
PullRequest.Body:
fix #349975

In Agent Host sessions with Assisted permissions, a request the reviewer marked as requiring approval skipped host permission evaluation entirely. That also ignored the rules saved by the "Allow … in this Session" and "Always Allow …" buttons on the prompt, so the same request prompted every time.

The request is now evaluated with only the rules the user saved, through the existing `getAutoApproval` path in a new `explicitRulesOnly` mode:

- Allow All and the implicit defaults (workspace reads and edits, the inline chat surface scope, terminal defaults) still defer to the reviewer.
- Deny rules, ask rules, protected writes and canonical path matching behave as before. Managed approval and sandbox-bypass requests are unchanged.
- Saved shell, URL and tool rules are honored as well as path rules. Saved shell rules must cover every sub-command, and a command that redirects into a file still prompts, because only the implicit workspace edit default could approve its destination.
- So that a shell grant chosen on such a prompt actually stops the repeat, the grants it offers also cover the sub-commands that terminal defaults approve. Those get exact rules, named in the grant's label, so a grant never overrides the defaults' deny rules for other forms of the command (for example `find -delete`). Inline chat, which confirms every shell command, and commands that only a redirect keeps from approval offer what they did before.
- In Assisted Autopilot a saved rule approves as host policy; other requests still report that no user is available.
- Re-evaluating a pending confirmation after a permission change gives the same answer as the initial evaluation.

A local window mirrors its URL approvals into the host's permissions, including the registered defaults when the user configured none. It now names those default rules in a new `defaultUrlAllowRules` root config value, read and sent together with the permissions, so they do not count as saved unless a chat or session holds the rule itself or the user grants it as Always Allow.

Section 8f of the Agent Host `AGENTS.md` is updated to match.

## How to test

Manually: start an Agent Host (Copilot) session with Assisted permissions, have the agent read a file outside the workspace so that the reviewer requires approval, choose "Always Allow Reading …", and trigger the same read again. It should run without a prompt, while a read of a different file outside the workspace still prompts. I did not run this signed-in flow; the evidence below is unit-level.

Commands run on macOS, with their results:

- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "vs/platform/agentHost/**/*.test.js"`: 18992 passing, 80 pending, 1 failing. The failure is an intermittent test in `sshProxyJump.test.ts`, which this change does not touch; that file passed in three reruns on its own.
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/**/*.test.js"`: 3929 passing, 2 pending, 0 failing
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `pnpm run oxlint` on the changed TypeScript files: no diagnostics
- `pnpm run valid-layers-check`: passed

The new regression tests in `sessionPermissions.test.ts`, `agentSideEffects.test.ts` and `agentHostCopilotCliSettingsContribution.test.ts` fail without the corresponding changes.

Not run: Windows and Linux, the full unit suite, and integration tests.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The early-return removal, awaited initial evaluation, unconditional write resolution, sequential sensitive-location loop, and serial pending-confirmation reevaluation are directly visible in the code. No saved allow means the eventual result is necessarily undefined. Filesystem latency and configuration size are unmeasured; the extra operations and critical-path placement are established statically.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Filesystem realpath and lstat operations for the write target and configured sensitive-edit locations.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For an ordinary write outside protected locations, each evaluation adds one target resolution plus K sensitive-location resolutions for the current single workspace root. Missing suffixes add ancestor realpath/lstat probes. A completed reevaluation of P such pending writes performs P*(1+K) resolutions serially across writes; subsequent triggers repeat them without application caching.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Additional filesystem latency on prompt/rejection delivery and head-of-line blocking of pending-approval reevaluation.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: After permission denials were checked, requiresUserConfirmation returned an empty decision without getAutoApproval. With an empty deny list, unattended rejection and pending reevaluation performed no path I/O. Interactive path-grant construction already resolved the target and sensitive locations; this PR adds a separate scan before that existing work.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Reviewer-required writes now enter getAutoApproval before publishing a prompt or returning the unattended rejection. With no saved allows, it still resolves the target and scans sensitive-edit locations before returning undefined; those checks cannot produce an approval in explicit-only mode.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: agentSideEffects.ts replaces the `e.managedApprovalRequired || e.requiresUserConfirmation` early return with a managed-only return and invokes getAutoApproval(..., { explicitRulesOnly: true }) at added line 1748. That newly reaches unconditional write-path resolution and protected-write checks even when the filtered saved allow list is empty.
Findings.Title: Skip filesystem scans when no saved allow can approve
Findings.Impact: An Assisted Autopilot write with no saved allow rules now waits for filesystem checks before reporting that approval is unavailable. On a network-mounted workspace, configured agent/hook locations add serial filesystem latency. Interactive prompts also gain an extra scan, and pending writes repeat it during reevaluation, delaying later eligible approvals.
Findings.Evidence: SessionPermissionManager.getAutoApproval resolves writeResources before checking whether any allow exists, then calls _requiresEditConfirmation when matchingAllowRules is empty. _matchesSensitiveEditLocations awaits _resolveResourcesForApproval for each configured location sequentially; _resolveResourcesForApproval uses realpath, with realpath/lstat ancestor walking for missing paths. AgentSideEffects._handleToolReady awaits this evaluation before its unattended branch and prompt construction. _reevaluatePendingConfirmations also awaits it sequentially for pending calls on every new prompt/configuration change.
Findings.Recommendation: In explicitRulesOnly mode, return undefined immediately after collecting saved permissions when allow is empty, before canonicalization or protected-write checks. For non-shell requests, also avoid protected-write scans once canonical matching establishes that no allow can approve. Keep the caller's deny check and all checks for potentially approving grants unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Deliver an Assisted write confirmation, or reject an unattended write, when no saved allow exists
Scenarios.CriticalPath: _handleToolReady awaits _evaluateHostPermission before publishing the interactive prompt or reaching the unattended rejection. Explicit-only evaluation resolves the write target and checks sensitive locations even though it cannot approve.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Canonicalize the write target and each sensitive-edit location using realpath, with lstat and parent walking for missing paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One target resolution plus K location resolutions per ordinary write evaluation; additional probes for missing suffixes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Reviewer-required requests skipped getAutoApproval after denial checks. With no deny rules, unattended rejection did no path I/O. Interactive path-option generation already performed its own resolution and sensitive-location scan; this evaluation adds a separate scan.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All resolutions finish before prompt delivery or unattended rejection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve canonical target/folder, inspect sensitive locations for writes, and search ancestors for .git.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For interactive nonprotected writes, target and folder resolution, K sensitive-location checks, and up to the target's ancestor depth in existence probes. Unattended requests do not reach this operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same interactive grant-generation operations already ran; no need to attribute those existing probes to this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing work must finish before publishing reusable grant options.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One requested write target and K deduplicated configured agent/hook locations. The current working-directory creation guard permits one root. An ordinary target outside those locations traverses all K; missing path components add ancestor probes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Independent initial requests may run concurrently; locations within one request are checked sequentially. No new global limiter or coalescing is supplied.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache or in-flight joining for canonical paths or sensitive locations. OS filesystem caches may reduce duration but do not eliminate issuance. Missing paths require realpath/lstat ancestor walking on every evaluation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: empty saved allows cannot approve, but unconditional target resolution and protected-write scans precede the explicit-only return.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Unmeasured filesystem latency and location count; slow network-mounted workspaces make the added serial work more consequential.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one medium-severity eager-work regression. Short-circuiting explicit-only evaluation with no saved allows preserves its decision while avoiding the added I/O.

Scenarios.Scenario: Honor saved read/edit grants while preserving asks, protected-write checks, and canonical path matching
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The SDK permission handler waits on its pending permission response. The host checks denials, evaluates the saved rules, and either responds directly or builds a prompt. Auto-approved requests strip confirmationTitle, so getPathConfirmationOptions returns without I/O.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve canonical target paths for denial and saved-allow matching, plus sensitive edit locations for non-exact write grants.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One target resolution for saved-allow matching; an additional target resolution if a nonmatching nonempty deny list requires canonical checking. Non-exact writes may add K location resolutions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Canonical denial checking already existed. Reviewer-required requests did not evaluate saved allows; instead they reached interactive grant generation and waited for a user. The added allow evaluation is necessary for the requested feature and can eliminate grant-generation I/O when approval succeeds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The requested tool waits until the host decision completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish the existing tool-ready/confirmation state to subscribed clients.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing action flow per permission signal, distributed to existing subscribers; not per permission rule.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same permission workflow already published tool state. The diff changes approval decisions rather than adding per-rule IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Makes the resulting tool status or prompt visible; SDK execution is released by the host response.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Deduplicated grants across chat, owner session, and host; one target per permission signal. Folder/wildcard edit grants may require K sensitive-location resolutions; exact absolute-file grants avoid that scan.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Initial permission requests are independent and can overlap. Checks within each evaluation preserve denial/ask/protected-write ordering; there is no per-file joining.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Rule lists are rebuilt from current configuration. Canonical filesystem checks are uncached, preserving live symlink behavior. Default URL markers are filtered against actual saved chat/session values.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the call path and counts. Necessary canonical checking for potentially approving grants is distinct from the reported no-allow case.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Grant counts, path latency, and incidence of protected edits are not measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: saved-rule matching requires these checks, and successful auto-approval removes existing prompt-generation work. Managed approval still exits before this new pass; sandbox bypass returns without filesystem checks.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reevaluate outstanding confirmations after a new prompt or permission/configuration change
Scenarios.CriticalPath: _reevaluatePendingConfirmations walks outstanding routes sequentially and awaits each host evaluation before considering the next prompt. An eligible later approval therefore waits behind earlier filesystem-bound writes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Repeat write-target canonicalization and sensitive-location checks for reviewer-required pending writes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A completed scan of P ordinary no-allow writes adds P*(1+K) canonical resolutions for one root, plus missing-path probes. Interrupted scans perform the reached prefix; no claim that every trigger completes a full scan.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Reviewer-required routes returned after denial checks. With an empty deny list, their reevaluation performed no path I/O. The scan, triggers, and cancellation placement themselves already existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serial checks block later eligible pending approvals. Cancellation does not stop an evaluation already in progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: P active pending permission routes across chats/sessions, each potentially containing K sensitive locations for its workspace. Every new prompt and every root/session/chat configuration event schedules a new scan.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One scan serializes its evaluations. Replacement cancels the previous scan, but cancellation is checked after the awaited evaluation, so already-issued filesystem work continues and old/new scans can temporarily overlap. This scheduling predates the PR.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cached approval decisions or canonical-path results. A permission change starts a fresh evaluation, and negative/no-allow decisions are not memoized.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the shared changed evaluator is used for initial requests and pending reevaluation, and the loop awaits each evaluation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneous pending prompts and configuration-event frequency vary. The repeated boundary work and serial head-of-line blocking are certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Same root cause as the submitted finding, not a second finding. Empty-allow short-circuiting removes the newly added work from these scans without changing reevaluation semantics.

Scenarios.Scenario: Evaluate Assisted shell requests and offer grants covering default-approved subcommands
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Permission evaluation and scoped option construction run before publishing a shell prompt. Tree-sitter evaluation is synchronous in the agent-host process; tool execution waits for the permission response.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse command text in WASM and classify subcommands under saved-only versus default-inclusive policy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For a reviewer-required unresolved shell request with no deny rules: one newly reached saved-only auto-approval parse and two option-evaluation parses rather than the previous single option parse. Pending reevaluation can repeat the saved-only parse. Each classification considers C commands against applicable saved rules.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Reviewer-required requests skipped host auto-approval; scoped options performed one default-inclusive evaluation. The second option evaluation now determines the exact extra rules required by the requested grant semantics.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous host CPU work precedes prompt publication or policy approval.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load WASM parser/grammars through the existing initialization path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Shared process-level initialization, including two grammar reads; not per permission request or subcommand.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same parser initialization and resource sharing already existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initialized before session events, not newly placed on the request critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Command text length, parsed subcommand count C, and deduplicated saved shell-rule count R. Grant construction includes distinct default-approved commands, not arbitrary workspace files.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Parsing uses the existing shared parser synchronously on the host event loop. Filesystem redirection checks remain parallel in ordinary mode; explicit-only mode returns noMatch without checking redirect destinations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Tree-sitter resources are initialized before session events and process-global resource loading is shared. Parsed trees are not cached; each evaluation creates/deletes its tree and query. Compiled default rules have a single identity-keyed cache; new empty objects can displace that entry.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in extra parses and existing resource lifecycle. Distinct policy classification is required by the new behavior; the no-saved-allow evaluation is covered by the submitted early-return direction.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Command lengths and parsing duration are not measured. No subprocess is launched by permission classification; actual shell execution remains downstream of approval.
Scenarios.Verdict: No independent finding beyond the reported empty-allow eager evaluation. Trees are deleted, resource loading is shared, and redirection filesystem checks are suppressed rather than fanned out in explicit-only mode.

Scenarios.Scenario: Evaluate saved URL and generic tool rules, distinguishing mirrored URL defaults
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Host permission matching must complete before responding to the pending request. This is in-memory configuration validation, deduplication, rule matching, and URL pattern comparison.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: A deduplicated allow list A and D registered-default URL markers. Saved chat/session rules form a Set; filtering uses defaultRules.includes, costing up to A*D comparisons. D comes from registered defaults when no global URL setting is configured, not an accumulating request history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous matching per request, followed by the existing asynchronous host decision promise. No per-URL network concurrency is created.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Current root/chat/session configuration is reread; no request-keyed retained cache is added. Default markers live as bounded configuration state and are removed when a host grant promotes a default into a saved rule.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed filtering is local computation and configuration-owned allocation; no network, database, subprocess, or per-rule IPC boundary was found.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Registered default count and user grant-list size are unmeasured. Inspected matching helpers do not fetch URLs or access the filesystem for URL/generic requests.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate reportable regression. The added metadata/filtering establishes provenance and does not by itself create expensive boundary fan-out or unbounded retention.

Scenarios.Scenario: Mirror local-window permissions/default markers and persist session or Always Allow grants
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The forwarder waits for a started host and advertised schema, computes both values synchronously before its await, and dispatches asynchronously. This does not add an awaited foreground UI startup step. Configuration publication precedes consumers seeing the new policy; persistence is queued separately.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the root configuration patch through the existing AHP dispatch notification.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One grouped permissions/default-marker action when either desired value changes; unchanged values send none. Other descriptor dispatches retain their existing count. A newly differing companion can cause a bounded action when permissions alone were equal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Permissions used the same dispatch path and structural guard. The diff adds a companion array to that action rather than one action for each default rule.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The host receives the changed policy through existing asynchronous publication; no per-rule round trip.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize the existing protocol action and persisted root configuration, now including default URL provenance when present.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing serialization per emitted action/persistence call; extra bytes scale with D default rules, not tool-input/history size.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same actions and root config were serialized without the default-marker field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Protocol encoding enables publication; persistent config encoding happens when the existing persistence path is invoked.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist root config using mkdir, write of a temporary file, then rename. Session grants use the existing session-config update path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing queued root write sequence per root update. Promoting an already-present default grant can newly require one bounded update; multiple grant rules remain grouped.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: New Always Allow grants and forwarded root changes already used this persistence path. The diff retains grouping and serialization, adding only bounded provenance state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Root writes execute on the existing promise chain and are not awaited by the permission evaluation or forwarder. Live policy changes publish before persistence finishes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed descriptor table, URL/terminal approval entries, saved rule arrays, and connected windows/subscribers. The default marker is a companion of the existing permissions descriptor, not another per-rule dispatch.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing per-descriptor _push calls can overlap. Permission/default values are grouped into one action. Host filesystem persistence is serialized by _rootConfigWrite; no new global subprocess or network burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Structural comparison suppresses unchanged actions, including companions. Schema-seen tracking retries only newly advertised managed keys; value-only state changes do not trigger cross-window reassertion. Default conversion is recomputed on the existing setting/start triggers and stored as configuration, not a growing event cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that atomic companion forwarding preserves one-action grouping, structural deduplication, schema gating, disposal, and the cross-window loop guard.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Window count, permission-list size, and write duration are unmeasured. Root updates transitively trigger existing session-policy publication and pending reevaluation; the newly costly no-allow write reevaluation is accounted for separately.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding for forwarding or persistence. Added configuration data does not establish harmful fan-out or unbounded allocation. The PR fixes repeated functional prompts, but no independently proven old performance-regression fix warrants blame provenance.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass against base 95fe7e433943b5cd8a152c6bdd22027147174e1c. Inspected all 10 changed files and every diff page, plus permission callers, canonical-path helpers, shell parser lifecycle, configuration forwarding, protocol dispatch, persistence, and supporting tests. Submitted one high-confidence medium-severity finding for newly awaited filesystem scans when no saved allow can approve; deduplicated its initial-request and pending-reevaluation impacts. No other concrete performance regression or qualifying regression-fix provenance established. Static read-only review; no profiling or execution.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
